title: upgrade from an older install says it cannot tell the direction, when both manifests' versions tell it: where the commits answer unknown, the versions decide (not in 0.1.16)
body:
`upgrade` from an install older than the vendored copy says it "cannot tell" which way it moves, when both manifests' versions tell it. On 2026-10-27 (intent-dc's read, AC-05.3's opt leg, Intent's transcript `refs/bank/dc/0087-05/out/ac053-opt.txt`, blob bd984b68fb40), `bin/devbin upgrade` in a project vendored from brew's 0.1.15 (4efb6e173e70), with the machine on an opt install of 0.1.14 (07f625a8c5e1), printed "cannot tell whether this source is ahead of or BEHIND what is vendored here". It went on, as upgrade does by design (issues 0021, 0053 and 0059: a rollback is warned, never refused), and reverted the runtime: 41 files updated, and 3 removed as no longer shipped (cmd/formula, cmd/macos, pages/formula.md). doctor in the same project named both versions. The direction is `unknown` because an install source is answered from its ancestry table (install_direction), written when 0.1.14 was published, which cannot know the later commit the project records. The version field both manifests carry answers it. Filed by vc on 2026-10-27; low, and not in 0.1.16.

## Fix

When the commits leave the direction `unknown` and both sides record a version that reads, the versions answer: a source whose version is lower than the vendored one is `backward`, and upgrade says it is BEHIND and will REVERT the runtime, naming both versions; a higher one is `forward`. Equal versions, or a version that does not read on either side, stay `unknown`, since a dev tree's version is not bumped per commit. The commits stay the first witness, and the version is read only where they cannot answer. One reader serves upgrade, the update notice, the offer and doctor, as source_direction does now.

## Done when

1. An arm in upgrade.bats vendors a project from an install at a later version, then upgrades it from an install at an earlier version whose ancestry cannot name the later commit. It reads the BEHIND line naming both versions, not "cannot tell". A second arm, at equal versions, still reads "cannot tell".
2. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU, with the tree scans and help, and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

- Where the commits cannot say which way a source moved, the versions do. source_direction asks the commits first, as before, and only where they answer `unknown` does it ask version_direction.
- version_direction compares the source's version (source_version: an install's manifest version, or a checkout's VERSION) with the one vendored. Higher is `forward`, lower is `backward`, and equal or unreadable stays `unknown`, since a dev tree's version is not bumped per commit. upgrade, vendor, the update notice, the offer and doctor all read it.
- upgrade's direction lines name both versions where both read: `devbin <here> vendored here, devbin <there> in this source`.
- Landed on main at c31e7b12, with the fix 5085ae24. The fix gives both arms a source with a committed VERSION (versioned_devsrc), since a fixture source carries none and its install recorded `unknown`.
- Arms in tests/unit/localinstall.bats:
  - "where the commits cannot say which way an install source moved, a lower version reads BEHIND, naming both versions (0276)";
  - "where the commits cannot say which way an install source moved and the versions are equal, upgrade still cannot tell (0276)", which now compares two equal X.Y.Z versions and holds the line naming both.
- Desk evidence:
  - hv's full run 20261029-1314 (2824 ok, 2 not ok) failed the BEHIND arm, `the install records no X.Y.Z version: unknown`, which 5085ae24 fixed.
  - Run 20261029-1336 ran it again after the fix: ok, 2 of 2 with its other red, its .errors empty.
  - hv's single run of the rewritten equal arm was ok, as vc read it.
